title: Canonical truncation filtration and shifted cohomology graded pieces
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $K$ be a cochain complex of $R$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] with $K^n=0$ outside a finite interval. Define a decreasing filtration by good upper truncations $F^iK=\tau_{\le -i}K$ [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category, def-sp-filtration]. Then $F^aK=K$ and $F^bK=0$ for suitable integers $a<b$, so $(K,F)$ is a finite filtered complex [def-kun-finite-filtered-module-homotopy]. For every $i$, the quotient $F^iK/F^{i+1}K$ [def-sp-filtered-complex-subquotients] is the two-term complex $\operatorname{im}(d^{-i-1})\hookrightarrow\ker(d^{-i})$ in degrees $-i-1,-i$, and the projection of cycles induces a natural quasi-isomorphism [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] $F^iK/F^{i+1}K\xrightarrow{\sim}H^{-i}(K)[i]$. These comparisons are natural for chain maps [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and a chain homotopy [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] between chain maps induces a filtration-preserving chain homotopy between their truncation maps. Consequently a quasi-isomorphism [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] $K\to L$ induces a quasi-isomorphism on every graded quotient.

source.place: Tag 0118 (good cochain truncations and their cohomology), together with Tag 05S6 and the canonical-truncation paragraph in Tag 0H7Z.

proof.text: Choose integers m≤n with K^r=0 for r<m and r>n. If i≤−n, then the cutoff −i is at least n; because the differential out of K^n has zero target, τ_{≤−i}K agrees with K in every degree. If i≥−m+1, then the cutoff is at most m−1 and every retained term is zero, so τ_{≤−i}K=0. Hence F^iK=K for i≤−n and F^iK=0 for i≥−m+1; the filtration is finite in the sense of [def-kun-finite-filtered-module-homotopy]. The inclusions τ_{≤−i−1}K⊆τ_{≤−i}K are subcomplex inclusions, so this is a decreasing filtration by subcomplexes.

source.place: Tag 0118, canonical truncation definition and its cohomology formula

proof.text: Fix i and put q=−i. The canonical truncation-step result [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-step-ses], applied in the abelian category of R-modules, identifies τ_{≤q}K/τ_{≤q−1}K with a complex supported in degrees q−1 and q: its degree-q−1 term is K^{q−1}/ker(d^{q−1}), its degree-q term is ker(d^q), and its differential is induced by d^{q−1}. The induced map from the first term to ker(d^q) is monic with image im(d^{q−1}); using the canonical coimage-image identification in an abelian category, this is the displayed two-term complex im(d^{q−1})↪ker(d^q). Since q=−i, this is F^iK/F^{i+1}K in degrees −i−1 and −i. The same result gives the natural quasi-isomorphism from this quotient to H^q(K)[−q]=H^{−i}(K)[i].

source.place: Remark 08J5 (successive canonical truncation triangle), with the degreewise quotient calculation from Homology Tag 0118

proof.text: For a chain map u:K→L, the truncation-step theorem's naturality clause says that u restricts to τ_{≤q}u and τ_{≤q−1}u and induces the corresponding map on the quotient, commuting with the projection to H^q(−)[−q]. Therefore the two-term-to-cohomology quasi-isomorphisms above are natural in u, and the induced map on the graded quotient is H^{−i}(u)[i] under the displayed identifications.

source.place: Remark 08J5 and canonical truncation functoriality; Homology Tag 0118

proof.text: If h is a chain homotopy from u to v, then h restricts to every truncation step. Indeed, for x∈(τ_{≤q}K)^r, if r<q the target degree r−1 is retained in τ_{≤q}L; if r=q then h^q(x) lies in L^{q−1}, which is again retained; and if r>q the source truncation term is zero. Thus h^r maps τ_{≤q}K^r into τ_{≤q}L^{r−1}. The identity u−v=dh+hd remains true after restriction because all truncations are subcomplexes. Hence truncation maps are connected by a filtration-preserving chain homotopy.

source.place: Tag 0118, degreewise definition of canonical truncations

proof.text: Finally let u:K→L be a quasi-isomorphism. By the natural identifications of Step 3, the map on the i-th graded quotient corresponds to H^{−i}(u)[i]. A quasi-isomorphism is, by definition, an isomorphism on every cohomology module, so H^{−i}(u)[i] is an isomorphism. Therefore every graded quotient map is a quasi-isomorphism, as required.
